scope.implemented: Thessa-owned ray-query reflection path for native scene objects: requested/resolved ray_tracing mode plus [raytracing] budgets and participation flags, negotiated EXPERIMENTAL_RAY_QUERY consent, fail-fast explicit requests, one BLAS per primitive over consolidated position/index copies, range-driven TLAS instances with custom_data pairing, camera-relative hit transform rows, a named reflection hook with an exactly-equal raster fallback, hit shading through the existing illumination model and shared shadow atlas, telemetry and deterministic GPU oracles
scope.not_implemented: terrain/ocean/atmosphere/cloud/landmark RT scene membership, RT shadow rays, texture/UV/normal/AO sampling in the hit path, alpha/transparent casters, temporal/spatial denoising, reservoir or ray-budget policy beyond one mirror sample, HDR/tonemapping/auto-exposure, mip chains, atmospheric indirect light, complete authored material/Bevy parity, prediction/reconciliation, external TCP/reconnect, FastRT ray-budget allocator/visibility correction
scope.ownership: MIT render-wgpu/ray_scene and render-core; GPL native scene/settings integration stays separate; the reflection hook is substituted by name, so no Bevy or wgpu type enters the semantic API
scope.new_gpu_work: one BLAS build per primitive and a TLAS build only when transforms/ranges/pairing change; zero acceleration-structure allocation, bind group or extra shader module when ray_tracing resolves off or specular_reflections is false

contracts.enablement: renderer.ray_tracing = off|local|full|auto. auto resolves local only when the adapter reports ray query before device creation. An explicit local/full request is never silently downgraded: the resolver keeps it, keeps the participation flags, and notes the limitation; Backend::bring_up_for_graphics then fails fast with BackendError::Device when the negotiated device lacks EXPERIMENTAL_RAY_QUERY. resolve_graphics re-resolves against the negotiated device so metadata describes the actual device.
contracts.fallback_equivalence: The raster substitute was exactly ambient/OCEAN_PI*fresnel*occlusion. The original miss oracle established byte identity only for a white metal (F0=1). Follow-up dielectric testing exposed that the RT miss multiplied an already-Fresnel-weighted environment by throughput, double-applying primary Fresnel. This is corrected and covered by dielectric/AO/roughness tests in native-environment-radiance-2026-10-17.json; the original oracle did not prove general miss equivalence.
contracts.scene_layout: A TLAS instance references a whole BLAS, so per-primitive instancing requires one BLAS per primitive; a single shared BLAS placed every primitive at every instance transform (observed as a real defect). Instances are the renderer's live mesh instances filtered by the existing per-primitive instance ranges. Primitives are flagged OPAQUE because a derived ray query has no any-hit stage: a non-opaque candidate intersection is never committed and the traversal then reports nothing at all.
contracts.hit_lookup: Instance custom_data carries the TLAS slot; a `pairs` storage buffer returns that slot's primitive index plus the three rows of its camera-relative 3x4 transform. Hit positions and normals are moved out of asset-local space by those rows instead of driver object-to-world conventions, and the primitive selects the material record and index/vertex range.
contracts.shading: Hit shading uses factor-only linear base color and metallic, a two-sided geometric normal and the existing illumination model (ambient plus per-light N.L with the shared cascaded shadow atlas). Stored hit roughness is unused. Textures and UVs are not sampled in hits. The chain is single-sample mirror specular faded by primary textured roughness and ROUGHNESS_CUTOFF = 0.6 to the isotropic environment term, bounded by reflection_bounces (default 2, clamped 1-4).
contracts.budget: raytracing.scene_memory_mib bounds a planning estimate - exact 16-byte vertex and 4-byte index copies plus bounded per-BLAS and per-instance terms - not the driver's own size query. A scene above the budget or above device limits is rejected with a reason instead of truncated.

reproduction.hardware: AMD Radeon 880M Graphics (RADV STRIX1), Vulkan; adapter reports mesh shaders and ray query present; same development machine as the surface-lighting baseline
reproduction.audio: Native has no audio subsystem. Test and app runs used ALSA_CONFIG_PATH=target/render-batch/silent-alsa.conf, an inaccessible PULSE_SERVER and PIPEWIRE_REMOTE=thessa-test-no-audio; no system audio settings changed
reproduction.config_files: target/render-batch/rt-local.toml and rt-off.toml differ only in [renderer] ray_tracing = "local"|"off", both preset high with specular_reflections = true and shadows enabled

verification.execution_notes: Debugging records the two defects that made every ray miss or mis-shade: non-opaque BLAS geometry never commits a candidate intersection in a derived ray query, and a single shared BLAS placed all primitives at all instance transforms. Both are now pinned by tests. An earlier oracle assertion also contradicted the resolver's documented no-silent-downgrade contract for explicit RT on an incapable adapter and was corrected to assert the note plus retained participation flags. Hardware work ran on the real development adapter, sequentially; no remote CI or blind subjective review result is claimed
verification.not_run: unrelated ignored long CPU physics profiles; full production-client/effect parity acceptance; other-platform (Metal/D3D12/WebGPU) RT runtime checks; WAN/network reconnect

ray_query_oracles.reflection_replaces_environment_with_sce: pass: a mirror quad facing a red quad returns a red-dominant center pixel (red > 32, green/blue < 8) where the RT-off raster render is exactly black; also asserts rt_stats().instances == 2 after update and no rejection reason
ray_query_oracles.miss_reproduces_the_raster_environment_t: pass: with only the mirror instanced (every reflection ray leaves the scene) the RT frame is byte-identical to the raster frame, and the raster renderer reports zero acceleration-structure passes
ray_query_oracles.ray_tracing_off_publishes_no_acceleratio: pass: RT off reports inactive stats, zero passes, zero bytes and the environment-only reflection
ray_query_oracles.ray_query_contract_holds_on_this_stack: pass on this adapter: one-triangle BLAS with a translation-only row-major 3x4 instance transform is hit at t = 1 with barycentrics (0.25, 0.25) after the transform, instance custom_data 7 round-trips, geometry index is 0 for a single-geometry BLAS. The probe uses a 16-byte vertex stride, matching the renderer
stack_behaviors_discovered: AccelerationStructureGeometryFlags::OPAQUE is required: without it the same probe reports kind = 0 (no intersection) on this driver, so every derived-query traversal silently misses
intersection.geometry_index is not usable to identify a primitive once several BLASes are instance-placed; the primitive must travel in instance custom_data

WGSL RayIntersection exposes geometry_index/primitive_index/instance_custom_data/barycentrics as implemented by naga 30.0.1 (field name `geometry` is rejected); lowering to SPIR-V follows the KHR ray-query instructions

fixed_source_measurement.scenario: 1280x720, screen-filling mirror quad plus a large target quad in its reflected direction over a 16-patch terrain and the shared 48 MiB / 12-pass shadow atlas; one device and one process, RT off then RT local, 30 warm-up + 120 measured frames, CPU encode/submit plus GPU completion (not isolated GPU timestamps, not game FPS)
fixed_source_measurement.delta_interpretation: worst-case per-pixel traversal plus hit shading (the hit path samples the shadow atlas); the acceleration structure is only four triangles, so this does not measure BVH-size scaling and is not a typical-scene cost
fixed_source_measurement.integrity_assertion: the probe fails unless the two configurations differ in more than 10,000 pixels; on this run all 921,600 pixels differ, so the traversal and hit shading are actually exercised. An earlier version of the probe measured an invisible result (hit fully shadow-occluded) and failed this assertion

captures.measured_noise_floor: same-config runs of the same capture command differ by 22-53 pixels at <= 5/255 on this machine (interleaved off-a/off-b and local-a/local-b pairs), while the RT-on/off difference is 38-51 pixels at <= 5/255: the captures are not deterministic at that level and the delta is indistinguishable from run-to-run noise
captures.physical_reason: Correction: the primary gate uses textured roughness (material.factors.y * metallic-roughness.G), not hit-record factors. Sampling 256x256 texels from each of the two 2048x2048 MR textures gives G medians 0.333/0.325, fractions below 0.6 of 0.999/1.000, B medians 0.000/0.000 and fractions above 0.5 of 0.035/0.146. The trace is eligible over essentially the whole primary surface; the earlier factor-roughness explanation was wrong. Mostly dielectric primary surfaces (F0 near 0.04), zero ambient environment and absent terrain/ocean RT membership are consistent with the tiny delta, not a measured attribution of individual changed pixels. Hit shading uses factors only: primary texture statistics cannot establish hit radiance.
captures.required_next_step: give the reflection term real content: a physical environment radiance field (single-scattering sky from the shared thessa-atmosphere optics) feeding the raster and RT environment terms plus a derived ambient, then texture/UV/normal/AO sampling in the RT hit path; the roughness gate itself is already textured and needs no change
captures.subjective_review: not performed; no blind aesthetic comparison, no invented ambient light to hide the dark captures

known_limits: Terrain, ocean, atmosphere, cloud and landmark geometry are not in the RT scene; raytracing.terrain/atmosphere/clouds remain participation flags without a consumer
No RT shadow rays: hit visibility comes from the raster shadow atlas, so hits outside valid covers are not occlusion-corrected
No texture/UV/normal/AO sampling in the hit path; no alpha or transparent casters; the hit record's RtSurface.roughness field is not consumed
Single mirror sample per bounce with a hard roughness cutoff; no denoising, reservoir reuse or ray-budget allocation policy
The scene memory budget is a planning estimate, not the driver's allocation; actual device memory is queried by the driver and only partly observable
No HDR/tonemapping/auto-exposure, mip chains or atmospheric indirect light (the last item is the follow-up slice this artifact's correction points to)
Ray tracing is a wgpu experimental feature behind thessa-wgpu-exp consent; other platforms (Metal/D3D12/WebGPU) have no runtime result here
The legacy Bevy client remains runnable; this slice does not declare the production client replaced
